solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Offensive work for soldiers getting hostile

indicators.note: 'work for soldiers' asks for one abbreviation to stand in the place of the other

parts.note: a synonym for disgusting or offensive
RE is the Royal Engineers, removed
OP is short for opus, a work, put in

explanation.surface: An army attack turns aggressive.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the RE at the start of REPUGNANT for OP to get OPPUGNANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Oppugnant is a rare literary word for opposing or antagonistic, a synonym of hostile.

clue.text: Partial withdrawals allowed in English town

indicators.note: partial means only part of the following words is used, the answer sitting inside them

parts.note: found running across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Some bank in a Midlands town lets customers take out only part of their money.
explanation.walkthrough: Walsall is a town in the West Midlands of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Walsall is an industrial town near Birmingham, so it is an example of an English town.

clue.text: First signs of paddock round-up uniting horses? This could be one

definitions.text: First signs of paddock round-up uniting horses? This could be one

indicators.note: the first signs of words are their opening letters, so only initials are kept

parts.note: the initial letter of each of these four words

explanation.surface: A groom gathers horses together in a field and wonders what call to use.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: PRUH is a Chambers word, a call to a horse or cow, just what you would shout while rounding up horses.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers lists pruh as an interjection used to call or steer animals, the very cry used when gathering horses.

clue.text: Shyest chap needing quiet? Could be this church member

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters might be rearranged into something else
needing here means lacking, so a letter goes missing from the words before it

parts.note: P, piano, is quiet in music; this letter is removed

explanation.surface: A very shy man who wants silence might suit some religious order.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove P from SHYEST CHAP and rearrange what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A hesychast was a mystic of the Eastern Orthodox Church practising inner stillness, so a member of that church.

clue.text: Poet's greatest hits?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: belonging to the Greek epic poet of the Iliad

definitions.note: plural noun, as the answer is
definitions.meaning: second meaning: home runs in baseball, the biggest hits a batter can make

explanation.surface: What are the best-known works of a famous poet?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greatest hits' suggests a best-of album, but here it is baseball slang for home runs.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's is the possessive of the Greek poet, and homers is American slang for home runs, the longest hits in baseball.

clue.text: Report including one chapter: Flowering Plant

indicators.note: including means one part holds the others within it

explanation.surface: A botanical report has a chapter on one flowering plant.
explanation.walkthrough: STATE goes round I and C.
explanation.definitionFit: Statice, or sea lavender, is a garden plant grown for its papery flowers.

clue.text: What's exposed after Sri Lanka hit

indicators.note: after places the first-named piece second, behind the country that follows it

parts.note: CL is Sri Lanka's international vehicle code, from Ceylon
outed means exposed or revealed publicly

explanation.surface: A news story about something revealed in the wake of a hit to Sri Lanka.
explanation.walkthrough: Sri Lanka was formerly Ceylon, which is why its vehicle code is CL.
explanation.definitionFit: To clout is to strike hard, so clouted is a past-tense synonym of hit.

clue.text: After shedding weight, shallow boat gets praise as before

indicators.note: shedding means losing something, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: a wherry is a light rowing boat or barge

explanation.surface: A light boat is lightened and wins compliments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as before' marks the definition as an old word: HERRY is obsolete Scots for to praise.
explanation.definitionFit: Herry is an archaic verb for to honour or glorify, so it is praise in older usage.

clue.text: Motion appearing right away to get poetic inspiration

indicators.note: motion means letters in movement, set to shift into a new order
away tells us one letter goes away and leaves the word

explanation.surface: A proposal suddenly appears, giving a poet a flash of an idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Motion' looks like a proposal at a meeting, but it signals movement of letters. Drop R from APPEARING and rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Aganippe was a spring on Mount Helicon sacred to the Muses, whose water inspired poets.

clue.text: The Oldie says it's coalfish

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the archaic form of says, as an old person might put it
second meaning: another name for the coley or coalfish

explanation.surface: The magazine The Oldie announces that something is coalfish.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oldie is a British magazine, but here it just means old-fashioned language.
explanation.definitionFit: Saith is the biblical form of says, and it is also a Scottish name for the coley, a fish of the cod family.

clue.text: Military detachment short of time using word of mouth

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so something is missing

parts.note: a patrol is a small detachment of soldiers

explanation.surface: A patrol low on time passes messages by mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: In law, parol evidence is oral rather than written.
explanation.definitionFit: Parol means given by spoken word rather than in writing, so it is a noun or adjective for oral statement.

clue.text: Wise to get permit on returning basic transport in Russia

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the whole is read from the end

explanation.surface: It is sensible to obtain a pass before going back to basic transport in Russia.
explanation.walkthrough: SAGE LET read backwards gives TELEGAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A telega is a crude four-wheeled Russian cart, so plural telegas are basic Russian vehicles.

clue.text: Lead start of project with back trouble

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, which alone is kept

parts.note: lumbago is pain in the lower back

explanation.surface: Someone leads a project while suffering from a bad back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' looks like a verb meaning to head, but it is the metal-like material graphite, once thought to be lead.
explanation.definitionFit: Plumbago is another name for graphite, the black lead of pencils, from Latin plumbum for lead.

clue.text: Set of railway wagons mentioned? Go for those in York

indicators.note: mentioned means spoken out, so we go by the sound of the word

parts.note: a rake is a string of railway carriages or wagons

explanation.surface: Is that line of goods wagons the one heading to York?
explanation.walkthrough: 'those in York' marks a Northern English and Scots dialect word: raik means to go or roam.
explanation.definitionFit: Raik is a Scots and Northern dialect verb meaning to go, range or wander.

clue.text: Self-assertive person wanting power, one puts others in their place

definitions.text: one puts others in their place

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so a letter is missing

explanation.surface: A pushy type loses influence and somebody else puts people in their place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'puts others in their place' sounds like a put-down, but it means showing people to their seats.
explanation.definitionFit: An usher shows guests to their seats at a theatre, wedding or church, literally seating them.

clue.text: Result in second act spoken of

indicators.note: spoken of means said out loud, so we rely on the sound of the words

parts.note: an act on a variety bill is a turn, and the second one is turn two

explanation.surface: Something happens as a consequence of the play's second act.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn to something is to become it, as when water turns to ice, so it means to end up as or result in.

clue.text: Cordially welcoming promenade in resort

indicators.note: resort read as re-sort means to sort again, putting letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A seaside resort's promenade with its friendly greeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' pretends to be a holiday town; read it as re-sort.
explanation.definitionFit: Open-armed describes greeting someone warmly with arms spread for an embrace, so cordial.

clue.text: Gearing adjusted, check to make a bit more powerful

definitions.text: check to make a bit more powerful

indicators.note: adjusted means altered, so the letters are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: A mechanic tweaks the gearing and checks it gives slightly more power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bit' is not a small amount but the horse's mouthpiece; the gag-rein tightens it.
explanation.definitionFit: A gag-rein is a rein arranged to pull the bit up into the horse's mouth, a check that makes it more severe.

clue.text: House member has Georgia replacing company for fraud

indicators.note: replacing means one item steps into the spot another held

parts.note: a member of the House of Commons

explanation.surface: An MP is found to have swapped Georgia for a firm in a fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: Put GA in place of the CO at the start of COMMONER.
explanation.definitionFit: To gammon is old slang for to hoax, so a gammoner is a deceiver or cheat.

clue.text: Swears about one form of therapy in forces

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one part goes round the other

explanation.surface: A soldier curses about a kind of treatment offered in the armed services.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forces' looks like the armed services, but it is a verb: effects means brings about.
explanation.definitionFit: To effect change is to cause or compel it, so effects works as a synonym of brings about by force.

clue.text: Low stool, Native American type

parts.note: the Cree are a Native American people
in printing, pie is jumbled type

explanation.surface: A short seat in a Native American style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'type' seems to mean kind, but in printing pie is type that has been mixed up.
explanation.definitionFit: A creepie is a Scots word for a small low stool, the kind used at a fireside.

clue.text: Study once more on King approaching term in prison

indicators.note: term means the end or limit, so only the final letter is kept

explanation.surface: A prisoner studies Shakespeare's King again while serving time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'term in prison' sounds like a sentence, but term means end, the last letter of prison.
explanation.definitionFit: To relearn is to learn something again, so to study it a second time.

clue.text: Intemperance sees service held up to some extent

indicators.note: in a down clue, held up means lifted so the letters run upwards
to some extent means only a portion of the words is used

parts.note: found running across these two words

explanation.surface: Heavy drinking sees a church service delayed for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: IVRESSE is the French word for drunkenness, used in English.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivresse means drunkenness, so it is a synonym for intemperance, excess drinking.

clue.text: Old tax sounding like member's payment

indicators.note: sounding like tells us to match the answer to how something is said

parts.note: an arm is a member of the body, and a fee is a payment

explanation.surface: A historic levy that sounds like a club subscription.
explanation.walkthrough: The match relies on a non-rhotic British accent, where arms and alms sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Almsfee was an old English church levy, Peter's pence, an example of a historic tax.

clue.text: Owns cracking image of stage in development

indicators.note: cracking means breaking into something, so one part goes inside another

explanation.surface: Someone has a striking picture showing a development stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Phasic is the adjective of phase, a stage in a process, so it relates to such a stage.

clue.text: Kind of pencil China exported for symbolic diagram

indicators.note: exported means sent out, so that word leaves

parts.note: a chinagraph pencil writes on glass and china

explanation.surface: A type of pencil that China sells abroad, used for diagrams.
explanation.walkthrough: A chinagraph is a wax pencil for marking glossy surfaces such as china.
explanation.definitionFit: A graph is a diagram plotting relations between quantities with symbols and lines.

clue.text: Pack he'd lead regularly?

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: Who usually leads the group?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: Akela is the leader of a Cub Scout pack, named after the wolf in The Jungle Book.
explanation.definitionFit: Akela is the title of the adult leader of a pack of Cub Scouts, who would lead it regularly.

clue.text: Dreamtime: Chronicles set in a long period of time

indicators.note: set in means placed inside something else

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Stories of the Dreamtime are told over a vast age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a long period of time' looks like one phrase but breaks into three parts; Chronicles is a book of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Alchera is the Aboriginal Australian word for the mythical Dreaming era of creation.

clue.text: Did nothing right in transactions with Germany

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one part sits within another

parts.note: TR is an abbreviation for transactions
D is Germany's international vehicle code
Chambers lists oke as a form of OK, meaning all right

explanation.surface: A trader's failure: nothing went right in dealings with Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transactions' looks like the definition's partner, but it is only an abbreviation; the answer is a Scots verb found in Chambers under truck.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers gives troke under truck, whose senses include dealing and loitering idly, so troked fits pottered or idled.

clue.text: Hunter car about to be reversed

indicators.note: reversed means turned round so the letters run backwards

parts.note: re means about, and it is turned round

explanation.surface: A hunter's car is about to be backed up.
explanation.definitionFit: A jager is a German rifleman or huntsman, from German Jäger meaning hunter.

clue.text: Fighter boxing Pole shown up for energy

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom
boxing means enclosing something, as a box does

parts.note: a MiG is a Russian fighter plane

explanation.surface: A boxer takes on a Polish opponent and turns up the vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: MiG is a Russian make of fighter jet; reversing it before or after the boxing gives the same letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Gism, or jism, is an informal word for force, spirit or vigour.

clue.text: What's backed in Aberdeen academy? It shouldn't be!

definitions.text: What's backed in Aberdeen academy? It shouldn't be!

indicators.note: backed means going backwards, so the letters are read from right to left
in means sitting inside the words that follow

parts.note: found across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: What a Scottish school supports, though it ought not to.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: schools once backed caning, and pupils were hit on the backside.
explanation.definitionFit: The cane was the rod schools used for corporal punishment, now banned, so it should not be endorsed.

clue.text: School group's distinctive practice showing discrimination

parts.note: a class is a group of pupils
an ism is a distinctive doctrine or practice

explanation.surface: A school's group has habits that turn out to be prejudiced.
explanation.definitionFit: Classism is prejudice against people because of their social class, a form of discrimination.

clue.text: Came to understand expression of hesitation for impure zinc

parts.note: Chambers gives spell as to make out or understand

explanation.surface: A chemist realises something, hesitates, and identifies a metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Spelter is commercial zinc containing impurities, used for castings and galvanising.

clue.text: Friendly goblin coming from kind of hut Norway's reserved

indicators.note: reserved means kept back, held apart, so it is left out

parts.note: a Nissen hut is a curved corrugated-iron shelter
N is Norway's international vehicle code, removed

explanation.surface: A kindly goblin emerges from a hut while Norway stays aloof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reserved' seems to describe a shy Norway, but it means set aside.
explanation.definitionFit: A nisse is a kindly household sprite of Scandinavian folklore, a type of goblin.

clue.text: Boastful about getting into charts I suspect

indicators.note: getting into means entering, so one part goes inside another
suspect means dubious, so the letters are not to be trusted as they stand

explanation.surface: Someone brags about entering the charts, I suspect.
explanation.walkthrough: Thraso is the bragging soldier in a comedy by Terence, which gives the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrasonic means bragging or vainglorious, a synonym for boastful.
